subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should trusted hook-agent requests be allowed to re-enter an existing stored session when they explicitly select persistent mode and pass the configured session-key policy?
rationale: Current session keys are routing identifiers rather than authorization boundaries, so source inspection cannot decide whether hook authentication plus allowed prefixes is the intended permanent authority model for durable-session access.

options.title: Approve scoped persistent mode
options.body: Allow explicit persistent mode for direct and mapped hook-agent requests while retaining isolated defaults and enforcing hook authentication plus allowed session-key prefixes.

options.title: Limit persistence to mappings
options.body: Permit persistent sessions only in operator-controlled mapping configuration and reject request- or transform-selected persistence to narrow the external authority surface.

options.title: Keep hooks isolated
options.body: Retain fresh sessions for all hook-agent calls and document that external integrations must use another authenticated session-entry API for continuity.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped persistent mode
recommendation.body: Allow explicit persistent mode for direct and mapped hook-agent requests while retaining isolated defaults and enforcing hook authentication plus allowed session-key prefixes.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue's prior review already framed the backward-compatible direction and the unresolved security question, making this the strongest available decision-routing signal.
